summary: Stale client-side confirmation cache causes duplicate external webhook invocations on retry
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports repeated duplicate POSTs to their external callback endpoint when the SDK performs retries after transient network failures. The duplicates correlate with SDK restarts and browser service-worker rehydration.

Impact: Customer is observing duplicated downstream side-effects (duplicate invoice generation) for a subset of streaming funcall flows. Affected tenant is on enterprise plan with private routing to their webhook. This is causing incorrect billing and manual reconciliation.

Environment: Production, us-east region. Customer uses both python backend workers (server-side) and a TS client (browser) that installs a service-worker proxy for offline/resume support. SDK versions: python-sdk@1.14.2, ts-sdk@2.3.0.

Observed timeframe: First reported 2026-03-09 18:40 UTC; recurring across multiple days.

Detailed description: The SDK emits a per-funcall idempotency confirmation token after the service acknowledges a tool/function call. The customer stores that confirmation locally to treat subsequent client replays as already-acknowledged. In their deployment the service-worker cache layer persisted confirmation tokens between client sessions, but did not expire or validate them against the server TTL. When a transient network blip caused the SDK to retry a portion of the request chain after a client restart, the client re-sent a stale confirmation header (previous run's token) while the server had purged the original confirmation entry (TTL expired). Server treated the header as a new confirmation and proceeded to re-emit the webhook to the customer's callback, resulting in duplicate callbacks.

Reproduction steps: See steps_to_reproduce for an exact sequence.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use TS SDK in browser with service-worker proxy that persists idempotency confirmations to IndexedDB.
2) Start a long-running funcall session that triggers an external webhook (tool call) and observe the webhook delivery succeeds once.
3) Let the confirmation TTL on server side expire (short TTL for testing) or restart the client process to simulate a session rehydrate.
4) Simulate a transient network failure that causes the SDK to retry the request chain after rehydration (e.g., disconnect and reconnect the client tab).
5) Observe that the client re-sends the stale confirmation token from IndexedDB; server-side confirmation lookup misses due to TTL; server treats flow as new and re-invokes the external webhook.
6) Verify duplicate side-effect on the customer's webhook endpoint and review request IDs in webhook payloads.

Expected behavior: Server should treat stale client-side cached confirmations as replay and avoid duplicate external webhook delivery, or client should not re-send confirmations that server has purged.
Actual behavior: Duplicate external webhook invocation occurs when client re-sends stale confirmations that no longer match server-side state.
logs: Customer supplied webhook logs and SDK debug logs. Example webhook POSTs show identical payload body but different x-rw-request-id headers: rw-req-20260309-abc123 and rw-req-20260309-abc123-retry. SDK trace shows 'confirmation-token: conf-7f9e' persisted in service-worker storage; server debug shows 'confirmation lookup: not found (expired)'.
investigation: Initial triage (Support): Confirmed duplicates map to same funcall flow and originate from client retries following client restart.
Reproduced in our staging with a minimal TS service-worker that persists confirmations to IndexedDB; reproduces within 2-3 retry cycles when server TTL is configured short.
Hypothesis 1: Client persists confirmation tokens across restarts without validating server TTL leading to stale token re-use.
Hypothesis 2: Server-side confirmation TTL/garbage-collection semantics are too aggressive and lack correlation checks when clients present old confirmations.
Logs: server audit shows 'confirmation-accepted' followed by webhook; later 'confirmation-missing' on retry path and webhook re-emitted. No duplicate-dedup index entry present because key expired.
SDK review: ts-sdk@2.3.0 stores confirmation tokens with no server TTL metadata; python-sdk persists to ephemeral memory only (not implicated).
Temporary mitigation validated: Instructing customer to purge service-worker confirmation store prevents duplicates immediately.
comments: 2026-03-10 20:05 UTC - Aisha Kapoor (Support): Hi team — customer reports duplicate webhooks after client restart. Attached logs and timing. Can engineering confirm if server should reject stale confirmations or return explicit 410 so SDK can purge?

2026-03-10 21:10 UTC - Ethan Miller (SRE): We can add a stricter server-side validation: when a confirmation token is presented but TTL expired, respond with 410 (Gone) and include expectedServerTTL header. Need SDK changes to handle 410 by purging local confirmation cache.

2026-03-11 09:30 UTC - Customer (Acme Health): We've purged service-worker cache and saw no duplicates in the last 8 hours. Would prefer a fix that doesn't require client-side surgery because multiple browser versions are in the wild.

2026-03-11 13:42 UTC - Dev (Ethan Miller): Created a quick-proof branch to change server confirmation lookup to return 410 + 'Confirmation-Expired' code when entry missing due to TTL. See PR: github.com/redwood/retry-middleware/pull/128. Need SDK owners to implement client-side handling for 410 to purge caches and avoid re-sending stale tokens.
2026-03-12 15:00 UTC - Support (Aisha Kapoor): Customer accepted temporary mitigation (manual purge) and asked for ETA on SDK patch. Assigned to SDK teams to prioritize.
root_cause: Client-side persistence of idempotency confirmations (service-worker IndexedDB) without awareness of server-side TTL allowed stale tokens to be re-sent after server-side entries were garbage-collected. The server currently accepts confirmation tokens if syntactically valid; when the server had already purged an entry, it treated the presented token as a new confirmation, causing duplicate outbound webhooks.
workaround: Customer-side: purge confirmation cache in the service-worker (IndexedDB) and deploy updated client that avoids persisting confirmations longer than session. Server-side temporary mitigation: return 410 when confirmation token is not found and include 'Confirmation-Status: expired' header so SDK can proactively purge stale entries.
resolution:
Partial mitigation pushed: server now returns 410 for expired confirmation tokens and adds 'Confirmation-Status: expired' header (rolled to canary in us-east on 2026-03-12). TS SDK owners requested to implement handling for 410 to purge local confirmation caches and to add a 'confirmation-ttl' field in future server responses. Customer performed manual purge and confirmed no new duplicates.

Follow-ups: 
- SDK TS team to add TTL-aware confirmation storage and purge-on-410 behavior (owner: @lina-chen; PR target: 2026-03-20).
- Add server-side instrumentation to log attempted replays against expired confirmations (owner: Ethan Miller; task ticket INT-3421).
- Update Developer Docs and best-practice guide on client confirmation storage and TTLs (owner: Developer Experience).
